If you haven't pushed this folder to GitHub before, here's the full flow. Takes 2 minutes.

### 1. Create the repo on GitHub
Go to github.com -> New repository -> give it a name like `tiny-sales-notebook` -> **Don't** check "add README". Create.

GitHub will show you a URL like: `https://github.com/yourname/tiny-sales-notebook.git`

### 2. In your terminal / VS Code terminal, go to your notebook folder
```bash
cd path/to/your/notebook-folder
```

### 3. Push it

Copy/paste these one by one:

```bash
# only needed the first time in this folder
git init

# add everything (your .ipynb, tiny_sales.csv)
git add .

# save a version
git commit -m "add today's notebook"

# rename branch to main
git branch -M main

# connect to GitHub - replace with YOUR url from step 1
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourname/tiny-sales-notebook.git

# push it up
git push -u origin main
```

It will ask you to log in - use your GitHub username and a Personal Access Token (not your password). GitHub will prompt you to create one if you don't have it.

### After today

Next time you just need 3 commands:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "update notebook"
git push
```

**Pro tip:** Create a `.gitignore` file in the folder so you don't push junk:

```
.ipynb_checkpoints/
__pycache__/
```

Want me to give you the commands for your specific notebook file name?
